details: Federal Reserve officials are signaling a shift from discussions of rate cuts to potentially even rate hikes if the conflict in Iran and the ongoing Strait of Hormuz blockade persist, which could fuel higher inflation. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has also revised down global growth forecasts and raised inflation projections, attributing these changes to escalating geopolitical tensions. In Europe, the energy crisis, intensified by the Iran conflict, is raising concerns about a potential euro zone recession, with the European Central Bank (ECB) acknowledging increased upside risks to inflation and downside risks to growth.
sourceName: IG, Investing.com, The Economic Times, Stat.ai
title: Geopolitical Tensions & Central Bank Stance Shifts Impact Global Markets

details: Bitcoin's price has exceeded $80,000, reaching a three-month high. This surge comes alongside significant daily inflows into Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), amounting to $630 million in a single day, and overall gains in Asian stock markets.
title: Bitcoin Surpasses $80,000 Amid Strong ETF Inflows

details: Brazil's central bank has issued new regulations forbidding electronic foreign exchange (eFX) companies from using cryptocurrencies for settling international remittances. These rules, effective October 1, mandate that payments between Brazilian eFX firms and their overseas counterparts must be processed through traditional foreign exchange transactions or nonresident real-denominated accounts.
title: Brazil Restricts Crypto for Overseas Remittances

details: A Reuters investigation revealed that Iran's Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) are actively using Nobitex, the country's largest crypto exchange, to convert dollars and circumvent U.S. sanctions. Nobitex has reportedly processed transactions worth hundreds of millions of dollars for sanctioned entities, establishing a parallel financial system outside traditional international banking.
title: Iran Utilizes Crypto Exchange to Bypass Sanctions
